title: A one-integer Postgres row takes 36 bytes of an 8 KB page, and a bigint row takes the same

steps.title: An empty 8 KB page has 8168 bytes free
steps.line: pd_lower 24 and pd_upper 8192 mark where free space starts and ends.
steps.caption: By default Postgres stores a table in pages of 8192 bytes, and every page starts with a 24-byte header. Two of its fields, pd_lower and pd_upper, mark where the free space starts and ends. On an empty page they are 24 and 8192, so 8168 bytes are free.
steps.picture: An 8192-byte page drawn top to bottom, not to scale: a 24-byte header, then free space.; 2 labels.

steps.title: One int4 row takes 36 bytes of the page
steps.line: A 4-byte line pointer, plus a 32-byte tuple at the page’s end.
steps.caption: An insert adds a 4-byte line pointer after the header and a tuple at the end of the page: a 23-byte header padded to 24, then the int4, 28 bytes. A 64-bit build stores each tuple in a multiple of 8 bytes, here 32, so a row costs 36 bytes.
steps.picture: An 8192-byte page drawn top to bottom, not to scale: a 24-byte header, then free space, then one 4-byte line pointer under the header and one 32-byte tuple at the very end of the page.; The 32-byte tuple in lines of 8 bytes, starting at offsets 0, 8, 16, 24: 23 header bytes, 1 padding byte, 4 data bytes, 4 padding bytes.; 4 labels.

steps.title: A full page holds 226 int4 rows; 11.0% of it is data
steps.line: Tuple headers take 63.5% of the page, more than the data.
steps.caption: Inserts fill the page until the next row no longer fits: 226 rows at the default fillfactor. The pie splits the 8192 bytes, with each part’s bytes in brackets. The 226 tuple headers take 63.5%, more than the 11.0% that is the values.
steps.picture: Pie chart “One page of int4 rows”: 6 slices; “int4, fillfactor 100”, 4 labelled values.

steps.title: Row 227 would need 32 bytes and a pointer; 32 are left
steps.line: Free space less a 4-byte pointer is 28 bytes, too few.
steps.caption: 226 rows of 36 bytes use 8136 of the 8168 free bytes, leaving 32; pageinspect reports pd_lower 928 and pd_upper 960. Before an insert, hio.c asks for the tuple’s 32 bytes, and bufpage.c counts the free space less a 4-byte pointer: 28 bytes, too few.
steps.picture: Pie chart “One page of int4 rows”: 6 slices; “Why 226 rows”, 6 labelled values. Too small for another row: Free space: 32 (0.4%). New in this step: “Why 226 rows”, 6 labelled values.

steps.title: An int8 row takes the same 36 bytes
steps.line: The 4 extra bytes fill the int4 tuple’s 4 bytes of padding.
steps.caption: The same pie, edited to int8: the data goes from 4 to 8 bytes a row. Its 4 extra bytes take the place of the 4 bytes of padding that rounded the int4 tuple from 28 up to 32. The slices change size; the page still holds 226 rows.
steps.picture: Pie chart “One page of int8 rows”: 6 slices; “Bytes”, 5 labelled values. Changed: Row data: 1808 (22.1%); Alignment padding: 226 (2.8%). New in this step: “Bytes”, 5 labelled values.

steps.title: Fillfactor 100, the default, holds nothing back: 226 rows
steps.line: Fillfactor 70 would hold 2457 bytes back and stop at 158 rows.
steps.caption: Back to int4. rel.h turns a table’s fillfactor into bytes an insert must leave free: 8192 x (100 - fillfactor) / 100, which is 0 at 100. So inserts fill the page to 226 rows. A table created with fillfactor 70 keeps 2457 bytes back and stops at 158.
steps.picture: Pie chart “One page of int4 rows”: 6 slices; “int4, fillfactor 100”, 5 labelled values. Nothing held back: Free space: 32 (0.4%). New in this step: Row data: 904 (11.0%); Alignment padding: 1130 (13.8%); “int4, fillfactor 100”, 5 labelled values.

steps.title: int4 and int8 fill 45 pages alike; with text after them, 55 and 64
steps.line: Both integer rows take 36 bytes; with text, 44 and 52.
steps.caption: Each line is a table of 10 000 rows at fillfactor 100, as measured on Postgres 18.6. int4 and int8 rows both take 36 bytes, so both tables take 45 pages. With an 11-character text column after the integer, the int8 table takes 64 pages to the int4 table’s 55.
steps.picture: “10 000 rows at fillfactor 100”, 4 labelled values. This case: int4: 36 bytes a row, 226 a page, 45 pages.
